p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram shows (a) the generation of fructose-6-phosphate from glucose-6-phosphate and (b) the steps in an elimination reaction. (a) The structure of glucose-6-phosphate is on the left. It consists of 6 carbons. The first 2 carbons on the left are shaded orange, along with their substituents. C1, which is numbered, bonds left to H and double bonds down to O, and right to C2, which is also numbered and bonds up to H and down to OH. These carbons and substituents are shaded orange. C2 bonds right to C3, which isn’t numbered, and which bonds up to OH and down to H, and right to C4. C4 bonds up to H and down to OH, then right to C5, which bonds up to H, down to OH, and right to C6. C6 bonds up to H, down to H, and right to O. O bonds right to P, which bonds up to O-, right to O-, and double bonds down to OH. To the right is an equilibrium arrow labeled phosphohexose isomerase in blue below it. To the right is the structure of fructose-6-phosphate. Its first 2 carbons are shaded orange. This is where the change occurs. C1 bonds left to H, up to H, and down to OH, then right to C2, which double bonds down to O and right to C. The rest of the chain is the same. Below is (b). The steps are numbered and bracketed, with a single illustration for each bracket. To the left is a vertically oriented molecule. 2 Cs are bonded horizontally. The C on the left bonds up to H, down to OH, and left to C. C double bonds down to O. The C and the double bonded O are shaded orange. Above is B1, which has 2 electrons, shown as red dots. A red arrow, representing electron transfer, comes down from B1 and points to H, which is shaded blue. Then an electron is transferred from the bond of the H down to the central C bond, then down from the double bond of the O to a blue shaded H on the bottom. The blue shaded H bonds down to B2, and transfers an electron to it. To the right, the steps of the reaction are indicated as such: (1) B1 abstracts a proton. (2) This allows the formation of a C-C double bond. (3) Electrons from carbonyl form an O—H bond with the hydrogen ion donated by B2. To the right there is a right arrow, followed by a long bracket. Inside the bracket are steps 4 and 5. The 2 carbons are now double bonded. The right C bonds down to O, which bonds down and right to H; the left C bonds down to O and down and left to H, which is shaded blue. At the bottom, B2 has 2 electrons on it. The electrons are transferred from B2 up to H by a red arrow, then from the H bond up to the C—O bond on the right. The electrons then transfer from the C—C double bond up to a now disconnected blue-shaded H, which is bonded up to B1 and transfers the electrons to it. On the right there are steps 4 and 5. Step 4 is on the bottom and step 5 is above it. They read: (4) B2 abstracts a proton, allowing the formation of a C---O bond. (5) An electron pair is displaced from the C—C bond to form a C—H bond with the proton donated by B1. The molecule is labeled enediol intermediate below. To the right is a closed bracket and another right arrow, pointing to the final product. The C on the right double bonds down to O (this is shaded orange) and right to C, which bonds up to a blue shaded H and down to OH, the H of which is shaded blue. Above there is B1, which has 2 electrons (red dots), and below is an H bonded down to B2.
